sourceTitle: 2026 工作趋势报告：员工的 AI 能力，需要组织制度接得住
originalTitle: Agents, human agency, and the opportunity for every organization

blocks.text: As AI and agents take on execution, our own agency expands.
blocks.zh: 随着AI和智能体执行处决,我们自己的机构正在扩大。
blocks.en: As AI and agents take on execution, our own agency expands.

blocks.text: The question is whether organizations are built to capture it.
blocks.zh: 问题在于是否建立组织来抓住它。
blocks.en: The question is whether organizations are built to capture it.

blocks.text: The opportunity for human potential at work has never been greater. People are using AI and agents to expand what they can do and who gets to do it, and new research shows that’s only accelerating. Call it the new agency equation: as agents take on more of the execution, humans increasingly have more agency—more room to direct the work, make the calls, and own the outcomes. For every firm, the imperative now is to turn that agency into unprecedented value.
blocks.zh: 发挥人的工作潜力的机会从未如此之大。人们利用人工智能和智能体 来扩大他们能做的和谁能做的并且新的研究表明,这只会加速。称之为新的机构方程式:当智能体承担更多的处决,人类越来越多地拥有更多的机构—— 更多的空间来指导工作,打电话,并拥有结果。对于每一个公司,现在必须把该机构变成前所未有的价值。
blocks.en: The opportunity for human potential at work has never been greater. People are using AI and agents to expand what they can do and who gets to do it, and new research shows that’s only accelerating. Call it the new agency equation: as agents take on more of the execution, humans increasingly have more agency—more room to direct the work, make the calls, and own the outcomes. For every firm, the imperative now is to turn that agency into unprecedented value.

blocks.text: We analyzed trillions of anonymized Microsoft 365 productivity signals and surveyed 20,000 workers using AI1 across 10 countries. We also spoke with leading experts in AI, work, and organizational psychology to help us unpack the insights from the data and understand where all this is going. The anxiety around AI at work is real—from fears of job loss to the pressure to keep up with rapidly evolving technology. But our research shows something else: that a growing share of workers are using AI in advanced, resourceful ways. The problem? Most organizations aren’t keeping up.
blocks.zh: 我们分析了数万亿的无名微软365生产力信号,并调查了10个国家的20 000名工人使用AI1的情况。我们还与大赦国际的主要专家进行了交谈,工作时,和组织的心理学 帮助我们解开 洞察力 从数据 和了解这一切的去向。AI在工作中的焦虑是真实的——从担心失业到跟上迅速发展的技术的压力.但是,我们的研究表明,其他的东西:越来越多的工人在高级阶段使用AI,聪明的方法。问题?多数组织没有跟上。
blocks.en: We analyzed trillions of anonymized Microsoft 365 productivity signals and surveyed 20,000 workers using AI1 across 10 countries. We also spoke with leading experts in AI, work, and organizational psychology to help us unpack the insights from the data and understand where all this is going. The anxiety around AI at work is real—from fears of job loss to the pressure to keep up with rapidly evolving technology. But our research shows something else: that a growing share of workers are using AI in advanced, resourceful ways. The problem? Most organizations aren’t keeping up.

blocks.text: In many cases, people are ready. The systems around them are not.
blocks.zh: 在许多情况下,人们都准备好了。他们周围的系统不是。
blocks.en: In many cases, people are ready. The systems around them are not.

blocks.text: The constraint for most firms is the gap between what their employees can now do and what their organizations are built to support. Our data shows that organizational factors—culture, manager support, talent practices—account for twice the reported AI impact2 of individual effort alone.
blocks.zh: 多数公司的制约因素是其雇员现在能够做什么,而其组织是用来支助的。我们的数据显示,组织因素 - 文化,管理支持,人才做法——仅个人努力的人工智能影响2的两倍。
blocks.en: The constraint for most firms is the gap between what their employees can now do and what their organizations are built to support. Our data shows that organizational factors—culture, manager support, talent practices—account for twice the reported AI impact2 of individual effort alone.

blocks.text: Bridging that gap means redesigning the operating model across employees, leaders, and the organization. The ones already doing it—Frontier Firms—are pulling ahead fast. Employees are using AI to lift the ceiling on what they can do. Leaders are rearchitecting work itself, deciding what humans and AI do. And organizations are turning into Learning Systems—because the companies that learn fastest from their own work will be the ones that win.
blocks.zh: 缩小这一差距意味着重新设计整个雇员的业务模式,领导人,与组织。那些已经这样做了的——Frontier公司—— 正在快速前进。雇员正在利用AI解除他们所能做的上限.领导人正在重新抓工作本身,决定人类和AI做什么。各组织正在转向学习系统,因为从自己的工作中学习得最快的公司将是获胜的公司。
blocks.en: Bridging that gap means redesigning the operating model across employees, leaders, and the organization. The ones already doing it—Frontier Firms—are pulling ahead fast. Employees are using AI to lift the ceiling on what they can do. Leaders are rearchitecting work itself, deciding what humans and AI do. And organizations are turning into Learning Systems—because the companies that learn fastest from their own work will be the ones that win.

blocks.text: Here’s what Frontier Firms do differently—and how we can all take control of what comes next.
blocks.zh: 我们如何能控制接下来会发生的事情。
blocks.en: Here’s what Frontier Firms do differently—and how we can all take control of what comes next.

blocks.text: Employees
blocks.zh: 雇员
blocks.en: Employees

blocks.text: AI lifts the ceilingon individual potential
blocks.zh: AI 提升个人的天花板潜力
blocks.en: AI lifts the ceilingon individual potential

blocks.text: AI is expanding what we can do—and putting a premium on judgment, clarity of intent, and the design of work itself.
blocks.zh: AI正在扩大我们所能做的工作——并重视判断,明确意图,和工作的设计本身。
blocks.en: AI is expanding what we can do—and putting a premium on judgment, clarity of intent, and the design of work itself.

blocks.text: A privacy-preserving analysis of more than 100,000 chats in Microsoft 365 Copilot shows that 49% of all conversations support cognitive work—helping workers analyze information, solve problems, evaluate, and think creatively. The remainder splits among working with people (19%), finding information (15%), and producing work (17%).3
blocks.zh: 对Microsoft 365的10万次聊天进行隐私保留分析显示,49%的谈话支持认知工作——帮助工人分析信息,解决问题,评估,并创造性地思考。其余部分分为与人合作(19%),寻找信息(15%),生产(17%)3
blocks.en: A privacy-preserving analysis of more than 100,000 chats in Microsoft 365 Copilot shows that 49% of all conversations support cognitive work—helping workers analyze information, solve problems, evaluate, and think creatively. The remainder splits among working with people (19%), finding information (15%), and producing work (17%).3

blocks.text: From expertise to agency
blocks.zh: 从专门知识到机构
blocks.en: From expertise to agency

blocks.text: AI expands who can do high-value work
blocks.zh: AI扩展谁能做高价值的工作
blocks.en: AI expands who can do high-value work

blocks.text: Nearly half of Microsoft 365 Copilot chat use supports analysis, decisions, and problem-solving—the kind of high-value work that once required deep expertise. The rest helps people work with others (19%), produce outputs (17%), and find information (15%).
blocks.zh: 微软365的Copilot聊天方式中近一半支持分析,决定,和解决问题——这种高价值的工作曾经需要深入的专业知识。其他帮助人们与他人一起工作(19%),产出(17%),并寻找信息(15%)。
blocks.en: Nearly half of Microsoft 365 Copilot chat use supports analysis, decisions, and problem-solving—the kind of high-value work that once required deep expertise. The rest helps people work with others (19%), produce outputs (17%), and find information (15%).

blocks.text: Employees at every level now have a partner that helps them analyze, synthesize, and deepen their own expertise, while also building expertise in other areas. AI is not just helping us do things faster. It’s expanding who can do high-value work.
blocks.zh: 各级雇员现在都有一个合作伙伴,帮助他们进行分析,合成,并加深他们自己的专业知识,同时也在其他领域积累专门知识。AI不仅仅是帮助我们更快地做事情.它正在扩大谁能做高价值的工作。
blocks.en: Employees at every level now have a partner that helps them analyze, synthesize, and deepen their own expertise, while also building expertise in other areas. AI is not just helping us do things faster. It’s expanding who can do high-value work.

blocks.text: The data backs this up: 66% of AI users we surveyed4 say AI has allowed them to spend more time on high-value work and 58% say they’re producing work they couldn’t have a year ago.
blocks.zh: 数据证实了这一点:66%的人工智能用户4 说人工智能允许他们花更多时间从事高价值的工作, 58%的人说他们正在制作一年前无法拥有的作品。
blocks.en: The data backs this up: 66% of AI users we surveyed4 say AI has allowed them to spend more time on high-value work and 58% say they’re producing work they couldn’t have a year ago.

blocks.text: That rises to 80% among Frontier Professionals, the most advanced AI users in our research. Frontier Professionals use agents for multi-step workflows and building multi-agent systems. They routinely rethink workflows and identify where agents can augment or automate. And they participate in practices like creating shared AI standards for their team or organization. They represent a small but disproportionately valuable group: 16% of the AI users we surveyed.
blocks.zh: 这在边境专业人员中上升到80%,我们研究中最先进的AI用户.边疆专业人才利用代理开展多步工作流程,构建多代理系统.他们通常会重新思考工作流程,并找出哪些代理商可以增强或自动化.并且他们参与一些实践,比如为他们团队或组织创建共同的AI标准.他们代表着一个很小但价值不高的群体:16%的人工智能用户 我们调查。
blocks.en: That rises to 80% among Frontier Professionals, the most advanced AI users in our research. Frontier Professionals use agents for multi-step workflows and building multi-agent systems. They routinely rethink workflows and identify where agents can augment or automate. And they participate in practices like creating shared AI standards for their team or organization. They represent a small but disproportionately valuable group: 16% of the AI users we surveyed.

blocks.text: Frontier Professionals refuse to outsource their thinking—they know long-term success means continuing to build human skills and not letting them atrophy.
blocks.zh: 边疆专业人员拒绝外包他们的思维——他们知道长期的成功意味着继续培养人的技能,而不让他们萎缩。
blocks.en: Frontier Professionals refuse to outsource their thinking—they know long-term success means continuing to build human skills and not letting them atrophy.

blocks.text: But as AI expands what people can do, it also raises the premium on good judgment. Most AI users we surveyed recognize this. Asked which human skills are more important as AI takes on more work, they said two topped the list: quality control of AI output (50%) and critical thinking—analyzing information objectively and making a reasoned judgment (46%). And 86% say they treat AI output as a starting point, not a final answer, and that they “stay responsible for the thinking.” They see their role is shifting from generating answers to evaluating, refining, and owning them.
blocks.zh: 但随着AI扩展人们能做的,这也提高了判断力的优势。我们调查的大多数人工智能用户都认识到这一点。有人问,随着AI从事更多的工作,哪些人的技能更为重要,他们说,两个居榜首:对人工智能产出(50%)和批判性思维进行质量控制——客观分析信息并作出合理判断(46%)。86%的人说他们把AI输出作为起点,这不是最后的答案,他们认为,他们的作用正在从产生答案转向评估,精炼,并拥有它们。
blocks.en: But as AI expands what people can do, it also raises the premium on good judgment. Most AI users we surveyed recognize this. Asked which human skills are more important as AI takes on more work, they said two topped the list: quality control of AI output (50%) and critical thinking—analyzing information objectively and making a reasoned judgment (46%). And 86% say they treat AI output as a starting point, not a final answer, and that they “stay responsible for the thinking.” They see their role is shifting from generating answers to evaluating, refining, and owning them.

blocks.text: Frontier Professionals are even more aware of the importance of human judgment when working with AI. They rank higher across every measure in the survey related to critical thinking and quality control—and that shows up in how they work. They are more likely than non-Frontier professionals to say they intentionally do some work without AI to keep their skills sharp (43% vs. 30%) and to say they intentionally pause before starting work to decide what should be done by AI versus a human (53% vs. 33%). Frontier Professionals refuse to outsource their thinking—they know long-term success means continuing to build human skills and not letting them atrophy.
blocks.zh: 边疆专业人员在与大赦国际合作时,更加意识到人类判断的重要性。他们在调查中涉及批判性思维和质量控制的每一项措施中排名较高,这表现在如何工作上。他们比非Frontier专业人士更有可能说,他们有意在没有AI的情况下做一些工作来保持自己的技能精锐(43%对.在开始工作之前,他们故意暂停,以决定AI对人应该做什么(53%对53%)。占33%).边疆专业人员拒绝外包他们的思维——他们知道长期的成功意味着继续培养人的技能,而不让他们萎缩。
blocks.en: Frontier Professionals are even more aware of the importance of human judgment when working with AI. They rank higher across every measure in the survey related to critical thinking and quality control—and that shows up in how they work. They are more likely than non-Frontier professionals to say they intentionally do some work without AI to keep their skills sharp (43% vs. 30%) and to say they intentionally pause before starting work to decide what should be done by AI versus a human (53% vs. 33%). Frontier Professionals refuse to outsource their thinking—they know long-term success means continuing to build human skills and not letting them atrophy.

blocks.text: The four modes of working with AI

blocks.en: The four modes of working with AI

blocks.text: How people work with AI depends on two things—how they engage with the work, and how much they use the agent. Four modes fall out: delegation, collaboration, asking, and exploration.
blocks.zh: 人们如何与AI合作 取决于两件事 - 他们如何参与工作,以及他们使用这个代理的多少。出现四种模式 :代表团,合作,问,和探索。
blocks.en: How people work with AI depends on two things—how they engage with the work, and how much they use the agent. Four modes fall out: delegation, collaboration, asking, and exploration.

blocks.en: Illustrative framework developed by the WTI 2026 research team, informed by patterns in Microsoft 365 Copilot usage and survey findings on how Frontier Professionals describe their AI work. blocks.text: As AI use matures across all employees, the most effective AI users won’t be the ones who do more things faster. They’ll be the ones who redefine their value around what only humans can do: setting clear intent—defining the desired outcome and quality bar—and designing how the work gets done across humans and AI. They apply judgment and taste, build trust, and shape systems that produce better outcomes. The question stops being “What tasks define my job?” and starts being “What outcomes am I now positioned to drive?”
blocks.zh: 由于AI对所有员工来说都是成熟的,最有效的人工智能用户不会更快地做更多的事情。他们将重新定义自己的价值,确定明确的意图——确定预期的结果和质量标准——并设计如何在人类和大赦国际之间开展工作。他们有裁判和口味,建立信任,并塑造能产生更好结果的系统。问题不再是“什么任务决定我的工作?” ,而是“我现在能够推动什么结果?”
blocks.en: As AI use matures across all employees, the most effective AI users won’t be the ones who do more things faster. They’ll be the ones who redefine their value around what only humans can do: setting clear intent—defining the desired outcome and quality bar—and designing how the work gets done across humans and AI. They apply judgment and taste, build trust, and shape systems that produce better outcomes. The question stops being “What tasks define my job?” and starts being “What outcomes am I now positioned to drive?”

blocks.text: Most organizations are not yet built to capture the value of this expanded human agency. The challenge is not isolated to tools or individuals—it’s a breakdown across the system that connects leadership, culture, management practices, and how work is measured.
blocks.zh: 大多数组织尚未建立起来,以抓住这一扩大的人类机构的价值。挑战并非孤立于工具或个人,而是整个系统的崩溃将领导阶层联系起来,文化,管理做法,和如何衡量工作。
blocks.en: Most organizations are not yet built to capture the value of this expanded human agency. The challenge is not isolated to tools or individuals—it’s a breakdown across the system that connects leadership, culture, management practices, and how work is measured.

blocks.text: To understand where this breakdown occurs, we mapped survey respondents across two dimensions: their capability with AI and their organization’s readiness to absorb it.
blocks.zh: 为了了解这种破裂的发生地点,我们绘制了两个方面的调查答卷人图:他们拥有AI的能力,他们组织也愿意吸收它。
blocks.en: To understand where this breakdown occurs, we mapped survey respondents across two dimensions: their capability with AI and their organization’s readiness to absorb it.

blocks.text: In many cases, employees are moving faster than the organizations around them.
blocks.zh: 在许多情况下,员工的移动速度比周围的组织要快。
blocks.en: In many cases, employees are moving faster than the organizations around them.

blocks.text: Individual capability reflects how broadly respondents report using AI and how confidently they direct it, judge its output, and learn from it. It also includes how actively they experiment and share learnings, and whether they report creating new value with AI—from improving work quality and processes to enabling work they couldn’t do before.
blocks.zh: 个人能力反映出受访者报告使用AI的广度,以及他们如何自信地指导它,判断它的产物,并且从中吸取教训。它还包括他们如何积极地进行实验和分享学习,从改善工作质量和工作流程到扶持他们以前无法完成的工作,
blocks.en: Individual capability reflects how broadly respondents report using AI and how confidently they direct it, judge its output, and learn from it. It also includes how actively they experiment and share learnings, and whether they report creating new value with AI—from improving work quality and processes to enabling work they couldn’t do before.

blocks.text: Organizational readiness reflects the environment around them, including: culture and management practices that support AI use, clear rules and guidelines for how people and AI work together, and whether AI use is encouraged and recognized.
blocks.zh: 组织准备就绪情况反映了周围的环境,包括:支持大赦国际使用的文化和管理做法;关于人们和大赦国际如何合作的明确规则和准则,以及大赦国际的使用是否得到鼓励和承认。
blocks.en: Organizational readiness reflects the environment around them, including: culture and management practices that support AI use, clear rules and guidelines for how people and AI work together, and whether AI use is encouraged and recognized.

blocks.text: The Transformation Paradox
blocks.zh: 变形参数
blocks.en: The Transformation Paradox

blocks.text: Workers are ready. Their organizations aren’t.
blocks.zh: 工人准备好了。他们的组织不是。
blocks.en: Workers are ready. Their organizations aren’t.

blocks.text: Roughly 1 in 5 workers are in the Frontier zone, where individual capability and organizational readiness reinforce each other. About 1 in 10 are blocked: skilled workers in companies that haven’t yet caught up. About half of all workers sit in the emergent zone in between.
blocks.zh: 大约五分之一的工人在边境地区,个人的能力和组织准备情况相互加强。大约十分之一被封锁:在尚未赶上的公司的熟练工人。大约一半的工人坐落在中间的新兴地区.
blocks.en: Roughly 1 in 5 workers are in the Frontier zone, where individual capability and organizational readiness reinforce each other. About 1 in 10 are blocked: skilled workers in companies that haven’t yet caught up. About half of all workers sit in the emergent zone in between.

blocks.text: The results reveal five groups of AI users. And in many cases, employees are moving faster than the organizations around them.
blocks.zh: 结果揭示了5组AI用户.在许多情况下,员工的移动速度比周围的组织要快。
blocks.en: The results reveal five groups of AI users. And in many cases, employees are moving faster than the organizations around them.

blocks.text: Only 19% of AI users are Frontier, the sweet spot where organizational capability and individual readiness are both high and reinforcing each other. At the other end, 16% are stalled, with low capability and limited organizational support. The rest are misaligned: 10% fall into blocked agency, where individuals have built strong skills but lack the systems to apply them. 5% sit in unclaimed capacity, where organizations are ready but employees have yet to catch up. The largest share sits in the messy middle, or emergent zone, where both individual practice and organizational conditions are still taking shape.
blocks.zh: 只有19%的人工智能用户是Frontier,组织能力和个人准备程度高、相互加强的甜点。在另一边,16%被困住了,能力低,组织支助有限。其余的错位:10%的人被封锁了· 个人培养了很强的技能,但缺乏应用这些技能的系统。5%的人以无人认领的身份,各组织已经做好准备,但雇员尚未赶上。最大的份额坐落在混乱的中间,或出现区,在个别做法和组织条件仍在形成的情况下。
blocks.en: Only 19% of AI users are Frontier, the sweet spot where organizational capability and individual readiness are both high and reinforcing each other. At the other end, 16% are stalled, with low capability and limited organizational support. The rest are misaligned: 10% fall into blocked agency, where individuals have built strong skills but lack the systems to apply them. 5% sit in unclaimed capacity, where organizations are ready but employees have yet to catch up. The largest share sits in the messy middle, or emergent zone, where both individual practice and organizational conditions are still taking shape.

blocks.text: This misalignment is reinforced at the top. Only one in four AI users surveyed (26%) say their leadership is clearly and consistently aligned on AI. Leaders surveyed are also more likely than employees to say AI-driven reinvention feels safe and rewarded.5
blocks.zh: 这种错位在顶部强化.只有四分之一接受调查的AI用户(26%)说,他们的领导地位明确和一致地与AI保持一致。接受调查的领导人也比雇员更有可能说AI驱动的革新感到安全和有回报。
blocks.en: This misalignment is reinforced at the top. Only one in four AI users surveyed (26%) say their leadership is clearly and consistently aligned on AI. Leaders surveyed are also more likely than employees to say AI-driven reinvention feels safe and rewarded.5

blocks.text: What emerges is a pressure point within the organization where the pull to perform collides with the push to transform. 65% of AI users fear falling behind if they don’t use AI to adapt quickly, yet 45% say it feels safer to focus on current goals than to redesign work with AI. And only 13% of AI users say they’re rewarded for reinvention of work with AI even if results aren’t met.
blocks.zh: 所出现的是组织内的压力点,在组织内,拉力执行与推动转变相碰撞.65%的AI用户担心若不使用AI迅速适应,但45%的人表示,关注当前目标比重新设计AI的工作更安全.也只有13%的人工智能用户表示,
blocks.en: What emerges is a pressure point within the organization where the pull to perform collides with the push to transform. 65% of AI users fear falling behind if they don’t use AI to adapt quickly, yet 45% say it feels safer to focus on current goals than to redesign work with AI. And only 13% of AI users say they’re rewarded for reinvention of work with AI even if results aren’t met.

blocks.text: We call this the Transformation Paradox: Employees are ready to reinvent how they work, but the system around them—metrics, incentives, and norms—continues to reinforce the old way. The same forces accelerating AI adoption are holding it back.
blocks.zh: 我们称这为"变形怪":员工们准备重新发明他们的工作方式,惟周围的系统是度量的,奖励;继续强化旧的方法。加速AI收养的同样力量正在阻止它.
blocks.en: We call this the Transformation Paradox: Employees are ready to reinvent how they work, but the system around them—metrics, incentives, and norms—continues to reinforce the old way. The same forces accelerating AI adoption are holding it back.

blocks.text: Leadership must redesign the system to match the work
blocks.zh: 领导必须重新设计系统,使之与工作相匹配
blocks.en: Leadership must redesign the system to match the work

blocks.text: The job of every leader right now is to make change stick. That means setting strategy at the top and ensuring the metrics, incentives, and expectations reward people for changing the way they work.
blocks.zh: 现在每个领导者的工作就是使变革成为现实。这意味着制定最高层的战略并确保衡量标准,奖励;和期望奖励人们 改变工作方式。
blocks.en: The job of every leader right now is to make change stick. That means setting strategy at the top and ensuring the metrics, incentives, and expectations reward people for changing the way they work.

blocks.text: Once that strategy is set, it’s managers who operationalize it, and the data shows the impact of their ability to do so.
blocks.zh: 一旦这个战略确定下来,是管理者操作它,这些数据显示了它们这样做的能力所产生的影响。
blocks.en: Once that strategy is set, it’s managers who operationalize it, and the data shows the impact of their ability to do so.

blocks.text: A separate Microsoft-led study6 of 1,800 workers globally found when managers actively modeled AI use, employees reported a 17-point lift in reported AI value7, a 22-point lift in critical thinking about their AI use, and a 30-point lift in trust in agentic AI. When managers created psychological safety around experimentation, employees reported up to 20 points higher AI readiness and value—and were 1.4x more likely to be high-frequency users of agentic AI.
blocks.zh: 由微软牵头对全球1,800名工人进行的一项单独研究6,当管理人员积极模拟AI使用时,雇员报告说,在报告的AI值7中有17点升空,22分的升降机 批判性思考他们的AI使用,和30点的升降 信任代理AI。当管理者在实验中创造心理安全雇员报告说,AI的准备程度和价值最高达20分,而且1.4x更可能是代理AI的高频用户。
blocks.en: A separate Microsoft-led study6 of 1,800 workers globally found when managers actively modeled AI use, employees reported a 17-point lift in reported AI value7, a 22-point lift in critical thinking about their AI use, and a 30-point lift in trust in agentic AI. When managers created psychological safety around experimentation, employees reported up to 20 points higher AI readiness and value—and were 1.4x more likely to be high-frequency users of agentic AI.

blocks.text: The Transformation Paradox is, at its core, a systems problem. And systems don’t fix themselves—they have to be redesigned.
blocks.zh: 变形怪是,在其核心,系统问题。系统无法自我修复,必须重新设计。
blocks.en: The Transformation Paradox is, at its core, a systems problem. And systems don’t fix themselves—they have to be redesigned.

blocks.text: Many leaders focus on hiring the right people and assume results will follow. But our data shows that it’s something else: the conditions leaders create for that talent to thrive.

blocks.text: The findings underscore the importance of an AI-ready environment: a culture that treats AI as a strategic advantage and encourages experimentation, managers who model and incentivize AI use, and talent practices that build skills and create space to apply them.

blocks.en: The findings underscore the importance of an AI-ready environment: a culture that treats AI as a strategic advantage and encourages experimentation, managers who model and incentivize AI use, and talent practices that build skills and create space to apply them.

blocks.text: The real question isn’t whether people have the right skills. It’s whether the organization is built to unlock them.

blocks.text: Building an evaluation infrastructure

blocks.en: Building an evaluation infrastructure

blocks.text: Creating those systems requires a disciplined approach to holding humans accountable for the work that agents execute. Many functions that deploy agents at scale will start to see a pattern: the more agents execute, the higher the stakes around human evaluation. Approving one bad output is manageable, but when bad outputs make it through at scale, the risk compounds. The key is to build an evaluation infrastructure that can keep up with agents.
blocks.zh: 建立这些系统需要采取纪律严明的做法,使人类对代理人执行的工作负责。许多在规模上部署代理的功能将开始看到一种模式:越多的智能体执行,人类评价的利害关系越大。批准一个糟糕的输出是可控的,但当不良的产物使它达到规模的时候,风险复合物。关键是建立一个能够跟上代理商的评价基础设施。
blocks.en: Creating those systems requires a disciplined approach to holding humans accountable for the work that agents execute. Many functions that deploy agents at scale will start to see a pattern: the more agents execute, the higher the stakes around human evaluation. Approving one bad output is manageable, but when bad outputs make it through at scale, the risk compounds. The key is to build an evaluation infrastructure that can keep up with agents.

blocks.text: It starts with three questions that every Frontier Firm will need to answer: Who reviews agent performance? Who has the authority to update the workflows that agents run? blocks.text: Building that infrastructure also requires coordinated reinvention across four roles: employees, who rearchitect their work around intent and review; leaders, who redesign processes around outcomes and agent autonomy; IT, who builds the infrastructure for agent operations at scale; and security, who ensures that trust is woven into the system itself.
blocks.zh: 建设这种基础设施还需要在以下四个方面进行协调的革新:雇员,(a) 围绕意图和审查重新安排其工作;领导人,由谁围绕成果和代理自主权重新设计流程;这,- 建设规模化代理业务的基础设施;与安全,他们确保把信任植入系统本身。
blocks.en: Building that infrastructure also requires coordinated reinvention across four roles: employees, who rearchitect their work around intent and review; leaders, who redesign processes around outcomes and agent autonomy; IT, who builds the infrastructure for agent operations at scale; and security, who ensures that trust is woven into the system itself.

blocks.text: For IT leaders, this means treating agents as managed entities with identities, permissions, policy enforcement, and lifecycle management. IT becomes the control plane for agent operations, extending the same rigor already applied to people and applications so that scale does not come at the cost of visibility.
blocks.zh: 对于IT领导者来说,这意味着将代理人视为具有身份的管理实体,权限,政策执行,和生命周期管理。它成为代理业务的控制飞机,扩大已经适用于人员和应用程序的同样的硬度,使尺度不以可见度为代价。
blocks.en: For IT leaders, this means treating agents as managed entities with identities, permissions, policy enforcement, and lifecycle management. IT becomes the control plane for agent operations, extending the same rigor already applied to people and applications so that scale does not come at the cost of visibility.

blocks.text: For security leaders, this means accounting for the new risk that agents introduce: data exfiltration, unintended system actions, and unauthorized access. Securing agents requires embedding monitoring, policy enforcement, and auditability directly into the platform, so that trust operates as a structural property of the system.

blocks.text: The firms that build a new operating model today won’t just move faster in the short term. They’ll build something more durable, setting themselves up to create value in ways that we can’t yet conceive of: an organization that learns faster than its competitors, compounds its own intelligence, and gets harder to catch with every cycle.

blocks.en: The firms that build a new operating model today won’t just move faster in the short term. blocks.text: This shift won’t happen easily. Some jobs will change. Some will go away. And many that don’t exist yet will emerge. According to LinkedIn’s 2026 Labor Market Report, in the past two years, employers have created at least 1.3 million AI-related job opportunities, which include data annotators, AI engineers, and forward-deployed engineers. These roles didn’t exist five years ago, but they have quickly become essential to digital economies. This kind of dynamism isn’t new to work, but the pace and scale of it are—and the uncertainty people feel is real.
blocks.zh: 这一转变不会轻易发生。有些工作会改变。有些会消失的而许多尚不存在的东西将会出现。根据LinkedIn的2026年劳动力市场报告,在过去两年中,雇主创造了至少130万个与AI有关的就业机会;包括数据注释员,AI工程师,和前方部署的工程师这些角色在五年前并不存在,但对于数字经济来说,它们已迅速变得至关重要。这种活力并不新鲜,但它的速度和规模, 和人们的不确定性是真实的。

These roles didn’t exist five years ago, but they have quickly become essential to digital economies. This kind of dynamism isn’t new to work, but the pace and scale of it are—and the uncertainty people feel is real.

blocks.text: What’s also real: The potential for employees to make impact has never been higher. Leaders are starting to redesign the systems around them. The organizations capturing what their work is teaching them are learning faster than the ones that aren’t. None of that happens by accident.

blocks.en: What’s also real: The potential for employees to make impact has never been higher. Leaders are starting to redesign the systems around them. The organizations capturing what their work is teaching them are learning faster than the ones that aren’t. None of that happens by accident.

blocks.text: The opportunity in front of every leader and organization is to take control: to build a place where agents amplify what people can do, where human judgment stays at the center of the work that matters, and where we all have the agency to decide what comes next. This is what AI can mean for all of us—if we choose to do the work to get there.

This is what AI can mean for all of us—if we choose to do the work to get there.

blocks.text: Frontier Professionals: To identify Frontier Professionals, we used a definition grounded in how people self-report how they are working with AI. Respondents were classified as Frontier Professionals only if they reported a combination of three distinct sets of behaviors: Advanced use of AI agents to complete complex or multi-step work; routine redesign of workflows to take advantage of what AI can do well; participation in structured, repeatable AI-enabled practices that can scale beyond individual use. They represent 3,233 of the 20,000 AI users surveyed. 44% are business decision makers, and 56% are employees. 50% are millennials, 23% Gen X, 22% Gen Z, and 4% Boomers. Frontier Professionals are more likely to work in tech (35%) or financial services (12%), with roles in IT (36%) or finance and accounting (11%). They tend to be in larger organizations (53% in companies with 500+ employees).

blocks.en: Frontier Professionals: To identify Frontier Professionals, we used a definition grounded in how people self-report how they are working with AI. Respondents were classified as Frontier Professionals only if they reported a combination of three distinct sets of behaviors: Advanced use of AI agents to complete complex or multi-step work; routine redesign of workflows to take advantage of what AI can do well; participation in structured, repeatable AI-enabled practices that can scale beyond individual use. They represent 3,233 of the 20,000 AI users surveyed. 44% are business decision makers, and 56% are employees. 50% are millennials, 23% Gen X, 22% Gen Z, and 4% Boomers. Frontier Professionals are more likely to work in tech (35%) or financial services (12%), with roles in IT (36%) or finance and accounting (11%). They tend to be in larger organizations (53% in companies with 500+ employees).

blocks.text: Organization vs. Employee AI Readiness Index: The Organization vs. Employee AI Readiness Index places each respondent on two self-reported dimensions: how ready they are as an individual to work with AI (a composite of usage sophistication, self-efficacy, proactive behaviors, and self-reported value creation) and how ready their organization is to support AI use (a composite of organizational AI culture, manager support, governance maturity, and AI in performance evaluation). Both dimensions are normalized 0 to 1 within each market before pooling. Each respondent is then assigned to one of five mutually exclusive zones: Frontier (clearly above median on both readiness dimensions, 19%), Blocked Agency (high individual, low organizational, 10%), Unclaimed Capacity (low individual, high organizational, 5%), Stalled (clearly below median on both, 16%), and the Emergent Zone (50%). The index is calculated on 16,971 respondents. Pearson correlation between the two readiness dimensions is r = 0.55.

blocks.text: AI Impact Analysis: The AI Impact Analysis identifies which of 29 measured factors are most strongly associated with workers reporting that AI is delivering real impact at work. The 29 factors are organized into three categories — organizational environment (10 factors describing the workplace), individual mindset and behavior (9 factors describing the worker's own orientation toward AI), and demographics (10 factors including job level, industry, market, generation, and AI familiarity). Importance is measured by random forest permutation, with cross-validation by elastic net regression and gradient-boosted trees. All three model families produce the same category ranking and the same top correlates, with held-out test R² of 0.680, 0.689, and 0.690 respectively. The analysis was run on 19,854 respondents, after removing respondents' missing values on any of the 29 factors. Every variable in the analysis is self-reported by the same respondent at the same moment, so the relationships shown are statistical associations, not causal effects.
